forecast-period.text: A high pressure ridge will be persistent over SA during the week, with a high moving across waters to the south to be centred over Victoria later Thursday and then over eastern NSW later Friday. The next cold front is likely to approach from the west late Saturday and move across SA on Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Cold at first with patchy frost about the Flinders Ranges and adjacent areas. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures below average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast during the day.
Isolated showers in the far northwest clearing overnight. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the coast and northern inland parts.

Cold at first with patchy fog and frost in parts, mainly on and to the east of the ranges. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average in the far southwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh and gusty in the northeast during the day.
Cold at first with patchy frost in parts of the east. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures above average. East to northeasterly winds, tending north to northwesterly about the southeast.

text.p: Dry and mostly sunny day. Slight chance of a shower or thunderstorm about the far southwest later. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds ahead of a change, freshening in the far west during the day. Winds freshening about the coast and shifting west to southwesterly from the west during the night.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: generally less than 2 mm across the Agricultural Areas. 5 to 10 mm possible in the far northwest, with local falls of 15 to 30 mm possible.
